nodes.name: Assumption 1, Assumption 3, Assumption 2, Assumption 4: Standing assumptions
nodes.statement:
There exists a constant \(\mu>0\) and a compact domain $\mathcal{V} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, both independent of $\theta$, such that for every \(\theta\in\Theta\), the function \(g(\theta,\cdot)\) satisfies the \(\texttt{P\L$^\circ$}\) condition.

There exist constants \(\rho>0\) and \(L_{g,3}<\infty\) such that for all \(\theta\in\Theta\),
\(g(\theta,\cdot)\) is \(\mathcal{C}^{3}\) on the tube \(\{x:\mathrm{dist}(x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))\le \rho\}\) and
\[
\sup_{\mathrm{dist}(x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))\le \rho}\ \big\|\nabla^3_{xxx}g(\theta,x)\big\|_{\mathrm{op}}\ \le\ L_{g,3}.
\]

For every $\theta\in\Theta$, the selected optimistic minimizer $x^\star(\theta)$ is unique and non-degenerate in the sense of 3.

The following statements hold for all \(\theta\in\Theta\).
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*]\setlength{\itemsep}{0.5pt}
\item \textbf{Regularity of \(f\).}
\(f\) is \(\mathcal{C}^{2}\) with respect to \((\theta,x)\). Moreover, \(f\) is \(L_{f,1}\)-Lipschitz and \(L_{f,2}\)-smooth with respect to \((\theta,x)\).
Since \(\Theta\) is compact, this global Lipschitz condition implies the derived linear-growth bound
\(|f(\theta,x)|\le C(1+\|x\|)\), uniformly over \(\theta\in\Theta\).

\item \textbf{Regularity of \(g\).}
\(g\) is \(\mathcal{C}^{3}\) with respect to \((\theta,x)\).
For every \(\theta\), the map \(x\mapsto g(\theta,x)\) is \(\mathcal{C}^{2}\) and \(L_{g,2}\)-smooth (i.e., \(\nabla_x g(\theta,\cdot)\) is \(L_{g,2}\)-Lipschitz).
Moreover, for all \(x\in\mathbb{R}^{d}\),
\[
\|\partial_{\theta}g(\theta,x)\| \;\le\; C_{g}\|x\|^{\mathsf{n}_{g}} + D_{g},
\]
for constants \(C_{g},D_{g}\ge 0\) and an integer \(\mathsf{n}_{g}\ge 1\).
We also assume polynomial growth of the mixed derivative used in the hyper-gradient:
\[
\|\nabla^2_{\theta x}g(\theta,x)\| \;\le\; C_{\theta x}\|x\|^{\mathsf{n}_{\theta x}} + D_{\theta x},
\]
for constants \(C_{\theta x},D_{\theta x}\ge 0\) and an integer \(\mathsf{n}_{\theta x}\ge 0\).

The Hessian \(\partial_x^2 g(\theta,x)\) is continuous with respect to \((\theta,x)\).

Moreover, there exist constants \(\mathsf{D}>0\) and \(\mu_{\mathsf{qg}}>0\) such that for all \(\|x\|\ge \mathsf{D}\),
\[
\frac{\mu_{\mathsf{qg}}}{2}\,\mathrm{dist}^{2}\!\bigl(x,\mathcal{S}(\theta)\bigr)
\;\le\;
g(\theta,x)-\min_{z\in\mathbb{R}^{d}} g(\theta,z).
\]
W.l.o.g.\ we take \(\mathsf{D}\) large enough so that \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\subseteq \mathbb B_d(0;\mathsf{D})\) for all \(\theta\in\Theta\).
\end{itemize}

nodes.name: Lemma 6: Tube radius ridge invertibility
nodes.statement:
Let 1, 3 hold.
Recall from 3 that \(\rho\) is the radius of the tube around \(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\) on which the
third-derivative bound \(L_{g,3}\) holds. Let \(\bar L_{g,3}:=\max\{L_{g,3},1\}\) and define
\[
r(\gamma):=\min\left\{\rho,\frac{\gamma}{2\bar L_{g,3}}\right\}.
\]
Then for all $\theta\in\Theta$ and all
$x\in\mathbb{R}^d$ satisfying $\mathrm{dist}(x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))\le r(\gamma)$, we have
\[
\nabla^2_{xx}g(\theta,x)+\gamma I \ \succeq\ \tfrac{\gamma}{2}\,I,
\qquad\text{and hence}\qquad
\big\|\big(\nabla^2_{xx}g(\theta,x)+\gamma I\big)^{-1}\big\|\ \le\ \tfrac{2}{\gamma}.
\]

nodes.name: Lemma 7: General stability bound
nodes.statement:
Let 1, 2, 4 hold, and let $x^\star:\Theta\to\mathbb{R}^d$ denote the unique optimistic
selection described above.
Fix \(\gamma>0\), an iteration $t$, a parameter $\theta_t\in\Theta$, and a candidate point $\tilde x_t\in\mathbb{R}^d$.
Let $\mathcal V\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ be any compact convex set containing $\{x^\star(\theta):\theta\in\Theta\}\cup\{\tilde x_t\}$.
Assume \(\nabla^2_{xx}g(\theta_t,\tilde x_t)+\gamma I\) is invertible and satisfies
\[
\big\|\big(\nabla^2_{xx}g(\theta_t,\tilde x_t)+\gamma I\big)^{-1}\big\|\le \kappa_\gamma .
\]
Let $\tilde v_t$ satisfy the residual bound
\[
\big\|\big(\nabla^2_{xx}g(\theta_t,\tilde x_t)+\gamma I\big)\tilde v_t-\nabla_x f(\theta_t,\tilde x_t)\big\|\ \le\ \eta_t.
\]
Define
\[
\widehat h_t
:=
\nabla_\theta f(\theta_t,\tilde x_t)-\nabla^2_{\theta x}g(\theta_t,\tilde x_t)\tilde v_t,
\qquad
e_t:=\widehat h_t-\nabla F(\theta_t).
\]
Then
\[
\|e_t\|\ \le\ C_x\Bigl(1+\kappa_\gamma+\frac{\kappa_\gamma}{c+\gamma}\Bigr)\,\|\tilde x_t-x^\star(\theta_t)\|
\ +\ C_{\mathrm{lin}}\cdot\kappa_\gamma\,\eta_t \ +\ C_{\mathrm{reg}}\cdot\gamma,
\]
where one admissible choice of constants is
\[
\begin{aligned}
C_{\mathrm{lin}}
&:=\sup_{(\theta,x)\in\Theta\times\mathcal V}\|\nabla^2_{\theta x}g(\theta,x)\|,\\[2pt]
C_x
&:=L_{\theta f,x} + L_{\theta x,x}\,B_{f,x} + B_{\theta x}\,L_{f_x,x} + B_{\theta x}\,L_{g_{xx},x}\,B_{f,x},\\
C_{\mathrm{reg}}
&:=\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}
\frac{\|\nabla^2_{\theta x}g(\theta,x^\star(\theta))\|\,\|\nabla_x f(\theta,x^\star(\theta))\|}{c^2},
\end{aligned}
\]
where $c>0$ is the normal spectral gap constant from 1,
\[
\begin{aligned}
B_{\theta x}
&:=\sup_{(\theta,x)\in\Theta\times\mathcal V}\|\nabla^2_{\theta x}g(\theta,x)\|,\qquad
B_{f,x}
:=\sup_{(\theta,x)\in\Theta\times\mathcal V}\|\nabla_x f(\theta,x)\|,
\end{aligned}
\]
and $L_{\theta f,x},L_{\theta x,x},L_{f_x,x},L_{g_{xx},x}<\infty$ are uniform Lipschitz constants on $\mathcal V$
(uniform over $\theta\in\Theta$) for
$x\mapsto \nabla_\theta f(\theta,x)$, $x\mapsto \nabla^2_{\theta x}g(\theta,x)$,
$x\mapsto \nabla_x f(\theta,x)$, and $x\mapsto \nabla^2_{xx}g(\theta,x)$, respectively.
Such constants exist and are finite because these maps are continuously differentiable and $\Theta\times\mathcal V$ is compact and convex.

nodes.name: Lemma 8: On-tube stability
nodes.statement:
Assume the hypotheses of Lemma~7 hold for the same \(\theta_t,\tilde x_t,\tilde v_t\), and fix $\gamma>0$ with tube radius $r(\gamma)$ from Lemma~6.
Let $\mathcal V=\mathbb B_d(0;\mathsf D+\rho)$.
Fix an iteration $t$ with $\theta_t\in\Theta$ and $\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x_t,\mathcal{S}(\theta_t))\le r(\gamma)$, so that $\tilde x_t\in\mathcal V$.
Assume clipping is inactive, i.e., the clipped vector used by the algorithm satisfies $v_t=\tilde v_t$.
Then the algorithmic hyper-gradient error $e_t=\widehat h_t-\nabla F(\theta_t)$ obeys
\[
\|e_t\|
\ \le\
A_\gamma\,\|\tilde x_t-x^\star(\theta_t)\|
\ +\ \tfrac{2C_{\mathrm{lin}}}{\gamma}\,\eta_t
\ +\ C_{\mathrm{reg}}\,\gamma,
\]
where $C_{\mathrm{lin}},C_{\mathrm{reg}}$ are as in Lemma~7 and
\[
A_\gamma
:=
C_x\Bigl(1+\tfrac{2}{\gamma}+\tfrac{2}{\gamma(c+\gamma)}\Bigr),
\]
with $c>0$ the normal spectral gap constant from 1 and $C_x$ as in Lemma~7.

nodes.name: Lemma 9: Off-tube moment control
nodes.statement:
Fix $\gamma>0$ and let \(r(\gamma)\) be the tube radius from Lemma~6.
Assume Algorithm~alg:hg-minsel-lmc uses the safeguard $v_t=\mathrm{Proj}_{\mathbb B_d(0;R_v)}(\tilde v_t)$, and assume the CG output $\tilde v_t$ satisfies $\|b_t-(H_t+\gamma I)\tilde v_t\|\le \eta_t$.
Let \(\mathsf{D}_{t}:=\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x_t,\mathcal{S}(\theta_t))\).
Define the tube event \(\mathcal E_t:=\{\mathsf{D}_{t}\le r(\gamma)\}\).
Under 4 and the smoothness of \(F\) on compact \(\Theta\), there exists a constant \(C_{\mathrm{off}}<\infty\), independent of \(t,\gamma,\eta_t,R_v\), such that
\[
\|e_t\|^2
\ \le\
C_{\mathrm{off}}(1+R_v^2)(1+\mathsf{D}_{t}^{2\mathsf n_{\theta x}}).
\]
Consequently,
\[
\mathbb E\big[\|e_t\|^2\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_t^c}\big]
\ \le\
C_{\mathrm{off}}(1+R_v^2)\,
\mathbb E\big[(1+\mathsf{D}_{t}^{2\mathsf n_{\theta x}})\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_t^c}\big].
\]
Moreover, on $\mathcal E_t$ Lemma~6 implies $\|\tilde v_t\|\le (2/\gamma)(L_{f,1}+\eta_t)$, so choosing
$R_v\ge (2/\gamma)(L_{f,1}+\eta_t)$ ensures the safeguard is inactive on $\mathcal E_t$ (i.e., $v_t=\tilde v_t$).

nodes.name: Lemma 1: Hyper-gradient error
nodes.statement:
Let 1, 3, 2, 4 hold.
Fix \(\gamma>0\), choose a tube radius \(r(\gamma)=\mathcal{O}(\gamma)\) as in 6, and define
\(\mathsf{D}_{t}:=\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x_t,\mathcal{S}(\theta_t))\) and
\(\mathcal E_t:=\{\mathsf{D}_{t}\le r(\gamma)\}\).
Choose the clipping radius in alg:hg-minsel-lmc so that
\(R_v=\mathcal{O}((L_{f,1}+\eta_t)/\gamma)\) as in 9.
Then for all \(t\),
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E\|e_t\|^2
&\le
3C_x^2\Big(1+\tfrac{2}{\gamma}+\tfrac{2}{\gamma(c+\gamma)}\Big)^{\!2}
\mathbb E\big[\|\tilde x_t-x^\star(\theta_t)\|^2\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_t}\big]\\
&\quad+\ \tfrac{12C_{\mathrm{lin}}^2}{\gamma^2}\,\eta_t^2
\ +\ 3C_{\mathrm{reg}}^2\,\gamma^2+\ C_{\mathrm{off}}(1+R_v^2)\,
\mathbb E\big[(1+\mathsf{D}_{t}^{2\mathsf n_{\theta x}})\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_t^c}\big],
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
where \(C_x,C_{\mathrm{lin}},C_{\mathrm{reg}}<\infty\) are stability constants depending on the global smoothness bounds
and the normal spectral gap of \(\nabla^2_{xx}g\) on \(\Theta\), \(c>0\) is the uniform normal spectral gap from
1, and \(C_{\mathrm{off}}<\infty\) depends on
\(C_{\theta x},D_{\theta x},\mathsf n_{\theta x}\) from 4.

nodes.name: Proposition 5: Curvature support
nodes.statement:
Let 1, 3 hold, and let \(c>0\) be the uniform normal spectral gap from
1. Fix any $\theta\in\Theta$. Then the second fundamental form $\mathrm{II}$ of $\mathcal{S}(\theta)$ satisfies
\[
\sup_{x\in \mathcal{S}(\theta)}\ \|\mathrm{II}_x\|_{\mathrm{op}}\ \le\ \frac{L_{g,3}}{c}.
\]
In particular, since \(L_{g,3}\) and \(c\) are uniform over \(\theta\in\Theta\), we obtain a uniform curvature bound over the family \(\{\mathcal{S}(\theta)\}_{\theta\in\Theta}\).

nodes.name: Lemma 10: Uniform growth of g
nodes.statement:
Let 1, 4 hold.
Then there exists a constant $\mu_{\mathrm{QG}}>0$ such that for all $\theta\in\Theta$ and all $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$,
\begin{equation}
g(\theta,x)-\min_{z\in\mathbb{R}^d}g(\theta,z)
\ \ge\
\frac{\mu_{\mathrm{QG}}}{2}\,\mathrm{dist}^2\!\bigl(x,\mathcal{S}(\theta)\bigr).
\end{equation}

nodes.name: Lemma 11: Gibbs tube concentration
nodes.statement:
Assume the setting of 10 and fix any $\theta\in\Theta$.
Let $X\sim \mu_\theta^\lambda$ and define $R:=\mathrm{dist}(X,\mathcal{S}(\theta))$.
Then there exist constants $\lambda_0,c_{\mathrm{tube}},C_{\mathrm{tube}},C_{\mathrm{tube},2}>0$ (independent of $\theta$ and $\lambda$) such that, for every \(0<\lambda\le\lambda_0\),
\begin{equation}
\mathbb P(R\ge t)\ \le\ C_{\mathrm{tube}}\exp\!\Big(-c_{\mathrm{tube}}\,\tfrac{t^2}{\lambda}\Big),
\qquad \forall t\ge 0.
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\[
\mathbb E[R]\le C_{\mathrm{tube}}\sqrt{\lambda},
\qquad
\mathbb E[R^2]\le C_{\mathrm{tube},2}\lambda.
\]

Moreover, if $X_1,\dots,X_M\stackrel{\mathrm{i.i.d.}}{\sim}\mu_\theta^\lambda$ and $\tilde x$ is any measurable selection of one of the candidates, then
\begin{equation}
\mathbb E\big[\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))\big]
\ \le\
\mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M}\mathrm{dist}(X_i,\mathcal{S}(\theta))\Big]
\ \le\
C_{\mathrm{tube}}\,\sqrt{\lambda\,\log(1+M)}.
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
\mathbb E\big[\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))^2\big]
\ \le\
\mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M}\mathrm{dist}(X_i,\mathcal{S}(\theta))^2\Big]
\ \le\
C_{\mathrm{tube},2}\,\lambda\,\log(1+M).
\end{equation}

nodes.name: Lemma 12: Candidate tube transfer
nodes.statement:
Assume the setting of 11. Let $X_1,\dots,X_M$ be candidates whose marginal laws
$\nu_1,\dots,\nu_M$ are not necessarily identical and satisfy
\[
\max_{1\le i\le M}R_2(\nu_i\|\mu_\theta^\lambda)\le \varepsilon_{\mathrm{R}}^2.
\]
Let $\tilde x$ be the hard-selection output
\[
\tilde x\in\arg\min_{1\le i\le M} f(\theta,X_i),
\]
with any measurable tie-breaking rule. Then
\begin{equation}
\mathbb P\!\Big(\max_{1\le i\le M}\mathrm{dist}(X_i,\mathcal{S}(\theta))\ge t\Big)
\le
M\,e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{R}}^2/2}\sqrt{C_{\mathrm{tube}}}
\exp\!\Big(-\tfrac{c_{\mathrm{tube}}}{2}\tfrac{t^2}{\lambda}\Big),
\qquad t\ge0.
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
\mathbb E\big[\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))\big]
\ \le\
\mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M}\mathrm{dist}(X_i,\mathcal{S}(\theta))\Big]
\ \le\
C_{\mathrm{tube}}\,e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{R}}^2/2}\sqrt{\lambda\,\log(1+M)},
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
\mathbb E\big[\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))^2\big]
\ \le\
\mathbb E\Big[\max_{1\le i\le M}\mathrm{dist}(X_i,\mathcal{S}(\theta))^2\Big]
\ \le\
C_{\mathrm{tube},2}\,e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{R}}^2/2}\lambda\,\log(1+M),
\end{equation}
after increasing \(C_{\mathrm{tube}}\) and \(C_{\mathrm{tube},2}\) by universal numerical factors if necessary.

nodes.name: Proposition 6: ULA R 'enyi mixing
nodes.statement:
Consider the unadjusted Langevin algorithm (ULA) iteration
\[
X^{k+1}=X^{k}-h\nabla G(X^{k})+\sqrt{2h}\,\xi^{k},
\qquad \xi^{k}\sim\mathcal N(0,I_d),
\]
targeting $\pi(\mathrm dx)\propto e^{-G(x)}\,\mathrm dx$.
Assume $\nabla G$ is $L_{G,2}$-Lipschitz and that $\pi$ satisfies a Poincar\'e inequality with constant $C_{\mathrm{PI}}$.
Let $\widehat\mu_n$ be the law of $X^{n}$.
Then for any sufficiently small $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ and an appropriate stepsize choice (as required by the ULA theory),
one can ensure $R_2(\widehat\mu_n\|\pi)\le \varepsilon^2$ after
\begin{equation}
n \;=\; \Theta\!\left(
C_{\mathrm{PI}}^{2}L_{G,2}^{2}\,d\,\varepsilon^{-2}\Big(R_3(\widehat\mu_0\|\pi)^2+\log^2(1/\varepsilon)\Big)
\right)
\end{equation}
iterations, where $R_q(\cdot\|\cdot)$ denotes the order-$q$ R\'enyi divergence.
Moreover, using the transportation-variance implication of the Poincar\'e inequality [liu2020poincare] to relate
\(W_2\) and \(R_2\), we obtain
\begin{equation}
\mathsf W_2(\widehat\mu_n,\pi)
\ \le\ 2\,C_{\mathrm{PI}}^{1/2}\,\big(e^{R_2(\widehat\mu_n\|\pi)}-1\big)^{1/2}
\ \le\ 2\,C_{\mathrm{PI}}^{1/2}\,C^{1/2}\,\varepsilon,
\end{equation}
where one may take the numerical constant $C:=2(e^{1/2}-1)$.

nodes.name: Corollary 1: R 'enyi transport control
nodes.statement:
Apply 6 with $G(x)=g(\theta,x)/\lambda$ and $\pi=\mu_\theta^\lambda$.
Then $L_{G,2}=L_{g,2}/\lambda$ and the ULA update
\[
X^{k+1}=X^{k}-h\nabla_x g(\theta,X^{k})+\sqrt{2\lambda h}\,\xi^{k}
\]
corresponds to the same ULA scheme with stepsize $h' = \lambda h$ for $G$.
In particular, for any target R\'enyi tolerance $\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}\in(0,1)$, running the chain for
\[
n
=
\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\!\left(
d\,C_{\mathrm{PI}}^{2}\lambda^{-2}\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}^{-2}
\bigl(1+R_3(\widehat\mu_0\|\mu_\theta^\lambda)^2\bigr)
\right)
\]
iterations ensures \(R_2(\widehat\mu_n\|\mu_\theta^\lambda)\le \varepsilon_{\mathrm R}^{2}\).
If, moreover, \(\widehat\mu_0=\widehat\mu_{0,z}^{\lambda}\) is the \(\lambda\)-scaled Gaussian initialization in
19 with \(z\in\mathcal Z\), then it suffices to run
\begin{equation}
n\ =\ \widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\!\left(d\,C_{\mathrm{PI}}^{2}\,\lambda^{-4}\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}^{-2}\right)
\end{equation}
iterations. If the Gaussian center satisfies \(z\in\mathcal{S}(\theta)\), then the sharper logarithmic bound
(41) gives the improved sufficient count
\[
n\ =\ \widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\!\left(d\,C_{\mathrm{PI}}^{2}\,\lambda^{-2}\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}^{-2}\right).
\]
In all cases, once
\[
R_2(\widehat\mu_n\|\mu_\theta^\lambda)\ \le\ \varepsilon_{\mathrm R}^{2},
\]
we have
\[
\mathsf W_2(\widehat\mu_n,\mu_\theta^\lambda)
\ \le\
2\sqrt{(e-1)C_{\mathrm{PI}}}\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm R},
\qquad\text{and hence}\qquad
\mathsf W_1(\widehat\mu_n,\mu_\theta^\lambda)
\ \le\
2\sqrt{(e-1)C_{\mathrm{PI}}}\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}.
\]

nodes.name: Definition 4: Lower-tail SQ
nodes.statement:
Let $Z$ be a real-valued random variable with (lower) quantile function
$q_u(Z):=\inf\{t\in\mathbb{R}:\ \mathbb{P}(Z\le t)\ge u\}$ for $u\in(0,1)$.
Define
\[
\mathrm{SQ}^{\mathrm{low}}_\delta(Z):=\frac1\delta\int_0^\delta q_u(Z)\,\delta u,
\qquad \delta\in(0,1).
\]
If $X\sim \nu$ and $Z=f(\theta,X)$, we also write
$\mathrm{SQ}^{\mathrm{low}}_\delta(f(\theta,X);\,X\sim\nu)$.

nodes.name: Lemma 13: Tail-min control
nodes.statement:
Fix $\theta$, candidates $X_1,\dots,X_M$, and $\delta\in(0,1)$. Let
\(
\tilde x \in \arg\min_{i\in[1:M]} f(\theta,X_i).
\)
Then
\[
f(\theta,\tilde x)\ \le\ \mathrm{SQ}^{\mathrm{low}}_\delta\big(f(\theta,X);\,X\sim\widehat\nu_M\big).
\]

nodes.name: Lemma 14: Hard-selection value gap
nodes.statement:
Fix $\theta$ and let $x^\star(\theta)$ be the unique minimizer of $f(\theta,\cdot)$ over $\mathcal{S}(\theta)$.
Assume \(\texttt{k}\ge1\) and that $x\mapsto f(\theta,x)$ is $L_{f,1}$-Lipschitz (as in 4).
Given candidates \(X_1,\ldots,X_M\), let
\[
\widehat\nu_M:=\frac1M\sum_{i=1}^M\delta_{X_i},
\qquad
\tilde x\in\arg\min_{1\le i\le M}f(\theta,X_i),
\]
with any measurable tie-breaking rule, and let $\bar x$ be any measurable Euclidean projection of \(\tilde x\) onto
\(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\).
Then, for every \(\delta\in(0,1)\),
\begin{align}
0 \ \le\ f(\theta,\bar x)-f(\theta,x^\star(\theta))
\ \le\ & L_{f,1}\,\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))
\\
&\quad + \Big[\mathrm{SQ}^{\mathrm{low}}_\delta\big(f(\theta,X);\,X\sim\widehat\nu_M\big)
	        - f(\theta,x^\star(\theta))\Big].

\end{align}
Moreover, for any reference measure $\nu$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with finite first moment,
\begin{align}
\mathrm{SQ}^{\mathrm{low}}_\delta\big(f(\theta,X);\,X\sim\widehat\nu_M\big)
- \mathrm{SQ}^{\mathrm{low}}_\delta\big(f(\theta,X);\,X\sim\nu\big)
\ \le\ \frac{L_{f,1}}{\delta}\;\mathsf{W}_1(\widehat\nu_M,\nu),

\end{align}
and consequently, choosing $\nu=\mu_\theta^\lambda$ yields
\begin{align}
f(\theta,\bar x)-f(\theta,x^\star(\theta))
\ \le\ & L_{f,1}\,\mathrm{dist}(\tilde x,\mathcal{S}(\theta))
\\
&\quad + \frac{L_{f,1}}{\delta}\;\mathsf{W}_1(\widehat\nu_M,\mu_\theta^\lambda)
+ \Big[\mathrm{SQ}^{\mathrm{low}}_\delta\big(f(\theta,X);\,X\sim\mu_\theta^\lambda\big)
	        - f(\theta,x^\star(\theta))\Big].

\end{align}

	Moreover, assume additionally that \(0<\lambda\le\lambda_0\), where \(\lambda_0\) is chosen small enough for both the
	tube bound in 11 and the projected-Gibbs small-ball bound used below, and that
	\(X_1,\dots,X_M\) are independent candidates with marginal laws
\(\nu_1,\dots,\nu_M\), that \(\mu_\theta^\lambda\) satisfies a Poincar\'e inequality with constant at most
\(C_{\mathrm{PI}}\), and that
\[
\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}^2:=\max_{1\le i\le M}R_2(\nu_i\|\mu_\theta^\lambda)<\infty.
\]
Assume \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}\le1\).
Then, for the hard-selection output \(\tilde x\) and projection \(\bar x\) defined above, there exists a constant
$C_1>0$ (depending only on the on-manifold geometry near $x^\star(\theta)$; under the uniform assumptions above it can be
chosen uniformly over \(\theta\)) such that
		\begin{equation}
		\mathbb E\big[f(\theta,\bar x)-F(\theta)\big]
		\ \le\
		2L_{f,1}\,C_{\mathrm{tube}}\,\sqrt{\lambda\log(1+M)}
		\ +\ C_1\,M^{-1/\texttt{k}}
		\ +\ 4\sqrt{e-1}\,L_{f,1}\sqrt{M\,C_{\mathrm{PI}}}\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm R},
		\end{equation}
		where $C_{\mathrm{tube}}$ is the tube constant from 11.

nodes.name: Lemma 15: Local growth on
nodes.statement:
Fix $\theta$ and suppose that $f(\theta,\cdot)$ is $\mathcal{C}^{2}$ in a neighborhood of $\mathcal{S}(\theta)$ and that
$x^\star(\theta)\in\mathcal{S}(\theta)$ is a local minimizer of \(f(\theta,\cdot)|_{\mathcal{S}(\theta)}\).
Assume moreover that the Riemannian Hessian of the restricted objective is positive definite at \(x^\star(\theta)\), i.e.,
there exists \(m_\theta>0\) such that
\[
\big\langle v,\mathrm{Hess}_{\mathcal{S}(\theta)}\bar f_\theta(x^\star(\theta))[v]\big\rangle
\ \ge\
m_\theta\|v\|^2,
\qquad
\forall v\in\mathcal{T}_{x^\star(\theta)}^\theta,
\]
where \(\bar f_\theta:=f(\theta,\cdot)|_{\mathcal{S}(\theta)}\).
Then there exist constants $c_{\mathrm{hg}}>0$ and $r_0>0$ such that for all $x\in\mathcal{S}(\theta)$ with
$d_{\mathcal{S}(\theta)}(x,x^\star(\theta))\le r_0$,
\begin{equation}
f(\theta,x)-f(\theta,x^\star(\theta))
\ \ge\
c_{\mathrm{hg}}\; d_{\mathcal{S}(\theta)}(x,x^\star(\theta))^2.
\end{equation}

nodes.name: Lemma 16: Uniform on-manifold growth
nodes.statement:
Assume the setting of 5 and let \(m_{\mathrm R}>0\) be the uniform restricted-curvature constant from
4.
Let $x^\star:\Theta\to\mathbb{R}^d$ be the global selected minimizer from 2.
Then there exist constants $c_{\mathrm{hg}}>0$ and $r_0>0$ such that for all $\theta\in\Theta$ and all
$x\in\mathcal{S}(\theta)$ with $d_{\mathcal{S}(\theta)}(x,x^\star(\theta))\le r_0$,
\[
f(\theta,x)-f(\theta,x^\star(\theta))
\ \ge\
c_{\mathrm{hg}}\; d_{\mathcal{S}(\theta)}(x,x^\star(\theta))^2.
\]

nodes.name: Lemma 17: Away-from-minimizer gap
nodes.statement:
Let $(c_{\mathrm{hg}},r_0)$ be the constants from 16 and define
\[
\mathcal{S}_{r_0}(\theta)
:=
\{x\in\mathcal{S}(\theta): d_{\mathcal{S}(\theta)}(x,x^\star(\theta))\ge r_0\},
\qquad
\Delta_{r_0}
:=
\inf_{\theta\in\Theta}\ \min_{x\in\mathcal{S}_{r_0}(\theta)}\big(f(\theta,x)-F(\theta)\big),
\]
with the convention that empty sets are ignored in the infimum. If all \(\mathcal{S}_{r_0}(\theta)\) are empty, choose any fixed positive value for \(\Delta_{r_0}\).
Then \(\Delta_{r_0}>0\).

nodes.name: Lemma 18: Value gap to distance
nodes.statement:
Let $(c_{\mathrm{hg}},r_0)$ be the constants from 16, and let \(\Delta_{r_0}>0\) be the uniform away-gap from 17.
Then for any $\theta\in\Theta$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E\|\bar x-x^\star(\theta)\|^2
&\ \le\
\Bigg(\frac{1}{c_{\mathrm{hg}}}+\frac{4\mathsf D^2}{\Delta_{r_0}}\Bigg)\,
\mathbb E\big[f(\theta,\bar x)-F(\theta)\big].
\end{aligned}
\]

nodes.name: Lemma 2: Selection error
nodes.statement:
Fix \(\theta\in\Theta\) and let \(x^\star(\theta)\) denote the unique minimizer of \(f(\theta,\cdot)\) over
\(\mathcal{S}(\theta)\). Assume 1, 3, 4, 2 hold, \(\texttt{k}\ge1\), and
\(0<\lambda\le\lambda_0\). Let \(X_1,\dots,X_N\) be the outputs of \(N\) independent finite-step ULA chains targeting
\(\mu_\theta^\lambda\), let \(\nu_i\) be the marginal law of \(X_i\), and write
\(\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}^2:=\max_{1\le i\le N}R_2(\nu_i\|\mu_\theta^\lambda)\). Assume
\(\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}\le1\), and let \(\tilde x\in\arg\min_{1\le i\le N}f(\theta,X_i)\) be the hard-selection output,
with a measurable tie-breaking rule.\footnote{For example, one may choose the smallest index among all candidates attaining
the minimum value of \(f(\theta,X_i)\), and set \(\tilde x\) to that candidate.} Then
\begin{align}
\mathbb E\|\tilde x-x^\star(\theta)\|^2
\ \le\ &
2e^{1/2}C_{\mathrm{tube},2}\,\lambda\log(1+N)\\
&\quad
+\ 2\Bigg(\frac{1}{c_{\mathrm{hg}}}+\frac{4\mathsf D^2}{\Delta_{r_0}}\Bigg)
\Bigg(
2L_{f,1}\,C_{\mathrm{tube}}\,\sqrt{\lambda\log(1+N)}
+\ C_1\,N^{-1/\texttt{k}}
\\
&\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad
+\ 4\sqrt{e-1}\,L_{f,1}\sqrt{N\,C_{\mathrm{PI}}}\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm R}
\Bigg).

\end{align}
The constants \(L_{f,1}\) and \(\mathsf D\) are from 4;
\(C_{\mathrm{PI}}\) is the low-temperature Poincar\'e constant from the discussion in Appendix~A.2;
\(C_{\mathrm{tube}}\), \(C_{\mathrm{tube},2}\), and \(\lambda_0\) are from
11, 12; \(C_1\) is from 14;
\(c_{\mathrm{hg}}\) and \(r_0\) are from 16; and \(\Delta_{r_0}>0\) is from
17.
